solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Referring maybe to crossing lacking interest

definitions.meaning: a ... crossing is a place where people on foot cross the road, so the word can describe such a crossing
... also means dull, prosaic or uninspired

explanation.surface: Someone talking about a road crossing is being dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian describes the familiar zebra-style crossing for walkers, and separately means plodding and unimaginative.

clue.text: A plot, brief, extraordinarily remunerative

indicators.note: something done extraordinarily is out of the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A short storyline that somehow pays very well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinarily' looks like it intensifies 'remunerative', but it signals rearranging the ten letters of A PLOT BRIEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something that brings in money or yields a good return.

clue.text: Expected of French to go around university

indicators.note: one piece is to be placed around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: de is French for of

explanation.surface: A French student was expected to visit a university.
explanation.definitionFit: Something due is anticipated or scheduled, as a train due at noon.

clue.text: Politician in delicatessen, a Tory

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician spotted shopping in a delicatessen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the answer is concealed across 'delicatessen, a Tory'; a Tory is a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, an elected or appointed legislator.

clue.text: Called about Channel Islands sports activity

indicators.note: the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: rang means telephoned, called
CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands, British islands off France

explanation.surface: Someone phoned to discuss a sport played in Jersey and Guernsey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Called' is past tense, telephoned, not named; the Channel Islands are Jersey, Guernsey and their neighbours.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing, of horses, cars or runners, is a competitive sport.

clue.text: Guy in outskirts of Airdrie building home

indicators.note: the first piece is placed in the second, inside it
the outskirts are the edges, so take the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: bod is informal British slang for a person, a guy

explanation.surface: A man on the edge of the Scottish town of Airdrie building his house.
explanation.walkthrough: Airdrie is a town near Glasgow; 'building' is only a link word joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An abode is a dwelling, the place where one lives.

clue.text: Silly urge in me for cake

indicators.note: silly means foolish or muddled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A foolish craving inside me for something sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' signals the anagram of URGE IN ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A meringue is a small light baked confection of whisked egg white and sugar, loosely a cake.

clue.text: Old Church article seen in the water

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An old church document turns up in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocean is the sea, which sailors call simply the water.

clue.text: Councillor conceals difficult situation, leading to ill humour

indicators.note: one piece hides another inside it

parts.note: to be in a hole is to be in a tight spot

explanation.surface: A local councillor hides an awkward predicament, which makes him bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Choler was one of the four humours, linked with anger, so it means irritability.

clue.text: Footballer George with, it's said, store of wine that's market success

parts.note: George Best was a famous Northern Irish footballer of Manchester United

indicators.note: the word is to be spoken, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: a cellar is where wine is stored

explanation.surface: A footballer's wine cellar being a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' turns CELLAR into its sound-alike SELLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bestseller is a book or product that sells in great numbers, a commercial hit.

clue.text: One parliamentarian, potential mischief-maker?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Is a single MP a likely troublemaker?
explanation.definitionFit: An imp is a small devil or a naughty child, someone given to mischief.

clue.text: Moment to introduce good news article initially evoking pity

indicators.note: letters are brought into the first piece, inside it

parts.note: a point is a moment in time, as at that point

indicators.note: take the first letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A time to share a piece of good news that is touching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives N and A from 'news article'; 'to introduce' puts G, N and A inside POINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Poignant means deeply moving, arousing sadness or sympathy.

clue.text: Fruit from Moroccan port

definitions.meaning: a small citrus fruit like a mandarin
a native of Tangier, the Moroccan port, or anything from there

explanation.definitionFit: The citrus is named after Tangier, so the adjective for that city doubles as the fruit.

clue.text: Arrive originally by means of railway to see bird enclosure

indicators.note: take the first letter, the one at the origin of the word

parts.note: via means by way of

explanation.surface: Arriving by train to visit an aviary.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviary is a large cage or building for keeping birds.

clue.text: Sweet tango dancing — Uruguay's first to enter

indicators.note: a letter goes into the other piece
dancing letters move about, so they are rearranged
take the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sweet tango with a Uruguayan joining in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' makes NOGAT from TANGO; 'first' gives U from Uruguay's, and 'to enter' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Nougat is a chewy confection of sugar or honey, nuts and egg white.

clue.text: Manage some cricket by bishop's place

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket
a see is a bishop's diocese or seat

explanation.surface: Running a cricket match next to a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise or direct the work of others.

clue.text: Cheers very short, beginning to need somewhere to drink!

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks, like cheers

indicators.note: a short word lacks its final letter
take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A quick toast and the urge for a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts VERY to VER; 'beginning to' gives N from need.
explanation.definitionFit: A tavern is an inn or pub, a place serving alcohol.

clue.text: Painting rocky place with sand

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady and shaken, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: A picture of a stony beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocky' signals rearranging PLACE and SAND together.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a picture of scenery, a genre of art.

clue.text: Quiet about group's reluctance to work

indicators.note: the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
a lot is a group or set; the 's is read as has, a link

explanation.surface: Keeping silent about a team's unwillingness to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth is laziness, one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Viewer, wise, savvy, astute in the end

indicators.note: take the final letter of each of the words

explanation.surface: A shrewd, perceptive observer, ultimately.
explanation.definitionFit: The eye is the organ one sees with, so it is the body's viewer.

clue.text: Revenue of popular company by this writer

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
the setter referring to himself gives me

explanation.surface: The earnings of a fashionable firm owned by the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Income is money received, earnings or revenue.

clue.text: Person welcoming English in Asian capital

indicators.note: one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: a soul is a person, as in not a soul

explanation.surface: Someone greeting an Englishman in an Asian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Seoul is the capital city of South Korea.

clue.text: Bird a little way along window ledge

indicators.note: the answer lies partway into the run of letters of the words

explanation.surface: A bird perched part way down the windowsill.
explanation.definitionFit: An owl is a nocturnal bird of prey.

clue.text: German leader's opportunity, getting backing of list of names

parts.note: a chance is an opportunity

indicators.note: backing means turned back to front, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a roll is a register of names

explanation.surface: The German head of government has a chance once a register supports them.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of leader's stands for has, a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Germany's head of government holds the title Chancellor.
